about: The vocabulary of recipe checks. A check is { kind, says, ...the fields its kind row names }. Adding a check kind is adding a row here: the validator reads every rule from the row. Field shapes: path = a list of keys starting at one of the roots (and reading only earlier steps); the `of` field of subset-of, covers and differs-from may also be a list of such paths, whose values are taken together, words = a non-empty list of non-empty strings, count = a whole number above 0, catalog = one of the catalogs, list = any list. A kind row's `wrong` is the binding whose value lists the values that break the rule (empty when it holds), and `holds`, when given, the binding that says whether it holds faster than `wrong` can; without `holds`, a rule holds when `wrong` is empty. In them {"$values": <field>, "transform"?} is the values at the rule's path in that field (the `this` root is the checked step's output; `values` stands in for `of` when the rule lists values instead), and {"$fill": <field>} is the rule's own value of that field. They are evaluated by the one shared evaluator every engine uses. A kind that has to look things up has `reads`: for each value of `each` the engine reads the address `from` builds from the value (the loop item), and {"$read": true, "transform"?} in its bindings is the list of what each read answered, a read that failed being {"tolerated_error": {"item": <the value>, ...}}. A kind whose `wrong` already says each break in words (`wrong_is_text`) is shown as it is; any other kind's values are shown as JSON.

roots.meaning: The output of the step the check belongs to.
The input the person gave the workflow.
The output of an earlier step; the key after it is that step's id.

catalogs.meaning: A workflow recipe the account can run.
A row in one of the account's lists.
A record in the account's data.
A task (calendar-task) that was taken and finished; the lookup answers the taker that finished it.

kinds.meaning: Every value at path is also a value at of (or at any of the paths of of, when of is a list of paths).
The values at path include every value at of (every path of it, when of is a list of paths), or every value listed in values.

Every item at path (a step's windows, each carrying the text it was asked for and the window read around it) holds its text exactly inside its window: the same characters, the same case and the same quote marks. An item whose window does not hold its text is a break, with the item's position named. Exact, not lowered: the same operator (op:core.contains, no lower step) that the formula engine's contains_exactly row is.
Every value at path appears in the text at in.
The text at path contains none of the listed words.

fields.refusal: must list the words to keep out.

kinds.meaning: The values at path hold at least count different values.

fields.refusal: must be a whole number above 0.

kinds.meaning: No value at path is also a value at of, such as a sending domain that must not be the main domain.
Every id at path names something that exists in the catalog.

Each lane of a step that has several agents is handed back with the id of its own job, and every such job ran, each finished by a different taker. The lanes are the step's own (its lanes, or its id and a place) and the number of agents is the step's agents.

fields.refusal: must name the field holding each lane's id.
must name the field holding each lane's job id.

then: the same taker finished more than one lane

kinds.meaning: Every item at path (a finding, a system, a row) carries each listed field with something in it: not missing, not null, not blank text, not an empty list or object. The failing values are `<item id>.<field>` for each missing one, so the refusal names what to add.

fields.refusal: must list the field names each item has to carry.

kinds.meaning: Every citation found in `field` of each item at path resolves, by the resolver rows of citation-resolvers.json: a code line holds the quoted text at the repository's ref, a commit exists and is dated after the item's `after` date, a row exists. An item with fewer than `at_least` citations fails. The failing values are `<item id>.<field>: <citation> (<why>)`. A resolver whose repository is not on the computer running the check leaves the check unevaluated, never passed.

fields.refusal: must name the field of each item that holds the citations.
must name a resolver row of citation-resolvers.json.
must name the field holding the text a cited code line has to contain.
must name the field holding the date a cited commit has to be after.
must be a whole number above 0.

kinds.meaning: In every item at path, the field named by `field` holds one of the listed values, such as an evidence kind that is a current measurement or a code read. The failing values are `<item id>.<field>`.

fields.refusal: must name the field to read in each item.
must list the values the field may hold.

kinds.meaning: Every row the step chose (each item at path names a row by its `row` and `type` fields) slots in through its own workflows: the row's `slot` field, read from the account, names one or more workflows, and each runs as a sub-run of this step whose id is made from this run, this step and the row (slottedRunKey). The check passes only when every such sub-run exists and every one of its steps has an answer kept after its own checks passed. The parent workflow names no format, template or row kind: a row with no workflow fails with `<row>: holds no workflow`, which is what the workflow that gives a row its workflows fills. The failing values are `<row>: <reason>` and `<row>: <sub-run id> (not finished)`.

fields.refusal: must name the field of each item holding the row's id.
must name the field of each item holding the row's type.
must name the row's own field that lists its workflows.
